compiled_state.title: Directory size monitor: advisory session-start hook with auto-ticketing
compiled_state.author: Claude
compiled_state.description:
## Context
Directories in DSO-managed repositories accumulate files over time, making navigation harder and increasing cognitive load. Today there is no mechanism to detect when a directory has grown unwieldy — tests/scripts currently has 351 files, tests/hooks has 157, and plugins/dso/scripts has 156. Developers and agents don't notice the gradual growth until a directory is deeply problematic. An advisory session-start hook that detects oversized directories and auto-creates backlog epic tickets ensures refactoring work is captured systematically without disrupting active workflows.

## Success Criteria
- A session-start hook scans all git-tracked files, counts files per directory, and identifies directories exceeding the configured threshold
- Directories matching .gitignore entries (via git ls-files), .git/, and a configurable exclusion list in dso-config.conf are excluded from scanning
- When a directory exceeds the threshold and no open ticket tagged dir:<path> exists, a P4 epic is auto-created with a descriptive title and the dir:<path> tag
- No duplicate tickets are created for the same directory — deduplication checks open tickets only, allowing re-flagging after a previous ticket is closed
- The hook prints an advisory summary of flagged directories to stderr without blocking session startup
- Threshold and exclusion list are configurable via dso-config.conf keys (directory_monitor.file_threshold default 30, directory_monitor.exclude_dirs default .git)

## Done Definitions
- When the directory monitor is active, starting a new session in a repo where tests/scripts/ has 351 files produces an advisory notice listing that directory as oversized
  <- Satisfies: "A session-start hook scans all git-tracked files, counts files per directory, and identifies directories exceeding the configured threshold"
- When the monitor detects an oversized directory with no existing open dir:<path> ticket, a new P4 epic appears in the ticket system with the dir:<path> tag
  <- Satisfies: "When a directory exceeds the threshold and no open ticket tagged dir:<path> exists, a P4 epic is auto-created"
- When a dir:<path> ticket already exists and is open, starting a new session does not create a duplicate ticket for that directory
  <- Satisfies: "No duplicate tickets are created for the same directory"
- When directory_monitor.file_threshold is set to 50 in dso-config.conf, directories with 40 files are not flagged
  <- Satisfies: "Threshold and exclusion list are configurable via dso-config.conf"
- When directory_monitor.exclude_dirs includes a directory path, that directory is not flagged regardless of file count
  <- Satisfies: "Directories matching .gitignore entries, .git/, and a configurable exclusion list are excluded"
- When the monitor runs, directories covered by .gitignore (like node_modules/) are not counted
  <- Satisfies: "Directories matching .gitignore entries (via git ls-files) are excluded"

## Scope
- IN: Session-start hook script, dso-config.conf keys, ticket auto-creation with dir:<path> tags, advisory stderr output, .gitignore-aware exclusion, configurable threshold and exclusion list
- OUT: Blocking commits or sessions, automatic directory refactoring, monitoring untracked files, recursive file counting (counts direct children only)

## Considerations
- [Testing] New hook script with ticket CLI integration — ensure tests cover dedup logic, threshold configuration, and exclusion filtering
- [Reliability] Hook depends on ticket CLI availability — implement graceful degradation if ticket commands fail
- [Performance] Small scale; no performance concerns for typical repos. Consider a scan timeout for unusually large repositories

## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)

### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The c2cc sprint installs the new session-start hook on the DSO repo itself and exercises it during the sprint. At least one session-start event during the c2cc sprint triggers the directory-size advisory hook AND the hook either (a) emits its no-issues confirmation or (b) auto-files an advisory ticket for an oversized directory it detected.

Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `test -x .claude/hooks/session-start-directory-size.sh` (or equivalent installed hook path) returns 0.
- Session transcript or `.claude/logs/session-start.log` (whatever artifact the hook produces) contains an entry from the current sprint session.
- If an advisory ticket was created: `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=directory-size-advisory --format=llm | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))"` returns ≥1. If no oversized directory existed, the no-issues confirmation appears in the session log.
## Dependencies
None

## Approach
Session-start hook script wired into the existing session-start dispatcher. Uses git ls-files (which naturally excludes .gitignore entries) piped through dirname/sort/uniq -c to count files per directory. Applies configurable exclusion list from dso-config.conf. For each directory over threshold, queries ticket system for open tickets tagged dir:<normalized-path>. Creates P4 epic if none found. Prints advisory summary to stderr.

## Scenario Analysis
- Threshold of 0 or 1 floods ticket system (medium, configuration): Setting the threshold to 0 or 1 causes every directory to trigger a ticket, creating dozens of epics in one session. Mitigation: enforce a minimum threshold or document the valid range.
- Exclude path format mismatch (medium, configuration): Path normalization differences between the exclusion list and the scanner could cause exclusions to silently fail. Mitigation: normalize paths before comparison.
